The king's movement in chess perfectly exemplifies this: it can move one square in any direction (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) in a single move, making all 8 adjacent squares equidistant at distance 1. This is fundamentally different from Manhattan distance (which would assign distance 2 to diagonal neighbors) or Euclidean distance (which would assign √2 ≈ 1.41 to diagonal neighbors). The question asks for "the name commonly used in mathematics," and "Chebyshev distance" is the standard mathematical term found in textbooks and literature, named after Pafnuty Chebyshev. While "L-infinity metric" is also mathematically correct and used in functional analysis, "Chebyshev distance" is the more direct and commonly cited name for this specific metric in general mathematics contexts.
